answer: The Copper-Kernel Sieve. 1) An auditor routes copper wire to incinerate an operational kernel chip per applicant. 2) The system registers each burnt chip as a unique vertex in a public graph. 3) The registry confirms exactly 50 burns for 50 passes. Cost for N identities equals 50 x N dollars, meaning 100 entries cost 5,000 dollars. The mechanism fails if a manufacturing breach drops kernel production costs to zero, allowing free burns. The irreversible incineration settles every record as if a furnace melted brass slugs into slag.
